reviewers.summary: The shell and navigation composition is present, but AC_006's test can pass without proving the required route handling. Case search also creates a duplicate browser history entry.

findingList.message: AC_006 does not prove route handling: its starting pathname already equals the expected finance home, so the required behavior can be absent while the path assertion passes. Use a starting route different from the role home and assert the expected final path.

evidence.codePathTraced: AC_006 starts at /work and later asserts that the final pathname is /work. If the unauthenticated redirect and sign-in return handling are removed, the browser can remain at /work and that pathname assertion still passes.
evidence.failureScenario: With no route guard or return handling, sign in from /work?returnTo=...; the test still sees pathname /work, so it does not prove the required allowed-route restoration or role-home fallback.

findingList.message: Case search adds the same history entry in both the App callback and CaseSearch, so one Back action leaves the user on the same case route.

evidence.codePathTraced: CaseSearch.submitMatch calls onNavigate(path) and then pushes that path itself. The new App callback handleCaseNavigate also calls history.pushState with the same path.
evidence.failureScenario: Submitting a case search pushes the case overview twice; pressing Back once returns to the same overview URL instead of the previous route.

reviewers.summary: The signed-in case content is rendered outside WorkspaceShell, contrary to the routing acceptance criterion. The AC_006 test also does not exercise restoration of an allowed returnTo path.

findingList.message: The shell does not contain the signed-in route content. Pass the case content into WorkspaceShell and add an assertion that the route content is inside its main region.

evidence.codePathTraced: When a session exists, App renders WorkspaceShell with an empty fragment as its child; the signed-in case section starts after WorkspaceShell closes at line 711.
evidence.failureScenario: A signed-in user opens a case route and sees the case content outside WorkspaceShell, so signed-in routes do not render inside the shell as required.

findingList.message: AC_006 requires restoring a valid route allowed for the signed-in role, but its named test covers only the disallowed-route fallback. Add a valid finance-reviewer returnTo case and assert the exact final path.

evidence.codePathTraced: AC_006_returnTo_and_role_route_integration supplies a returnTo path for findings, which is outside the finance-reviewer allowlist, and only asserts the /work fallback at line 293.
evidence.failureScenario: If sign-in always sends finance reviewers to /work, the named test still passes even when a valid allowed returnTo such as /cases/case-001/reserve is not restored.

reviewers.summary: The changed code includes role-based fallback handling, but the named integration test does not verify the allowed-route restoration required by AC_006. I found no concrete exploitable security vulnerability in the reviewed diff.

findingList.message: AC_006 requires restoring a valid route allowed for the signed-in role, but the named test covers only the disallowed-route fallback. Add a test case that starts from a valid finance-reviewer route and asserts the exact restored path.

evidence.codePathTraced: AC_006_returnTo_and_role_route_integration starts with an explicit returnTo to a findings route that is disallowed for the finance reviewer, then checks only that the final path is /work.
evidence.failureScenario: If the App drops a valid returnTo route that the signed-in role is allowed to access, this test still passes because it never exercises or asserts restoration of an allowed route.
